reasoning: The stem describes a client with type 1 diabetes who began a new 45-minute cycling routine without adjusting the preexisting meal and insulin plan, and who developed adrenergic and neuroglycopenic symptoms with CGM-confirmed glucose of 58 to 64 mg/dL only during or within one hour after cycling. Noncycling glucose is normal and there is no illness or ketones, so C3 (activity-associated hypoglycemia from a plan not aligned with the new exercise) fits best. A2 addresses the root cause by obtaining an individualized exercise-day carbohydrate and medication plan from the prescriber or DSMES team, and A3 ensures the client is prepared to promptly treat a low during the next ride. P1 tracks recurrence and timing of hypoglycemia, and P2 captures peri-exercise glucose patterns needed to evaluate the plan adjustment.
